content: 1. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal when discontinuing a CYP3A4 inducer. If the inducer is stopped, consider reducing the dosage of oliceridine and closely monitor for respiratory depression. 2. Rifampin reduces omeprazole levels or efficacy by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Rifampin decreases ondansetron levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 4. Rifampin reduces osilodrostat levels or efficacy by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Osilodrostat is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP2B6. Monitor for changes in efficacy or adverse effects during coadministration or discontinuation with strong CYP3A4 and/or CYP2B6 inducers. 5. Rifampin decreases ospemifene levels by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Rifampin reduces oxybutynin levels or efficacy by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Rifampin decreases oxycodone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Rifampin reduces paclitaxel levels or efficacy by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, and other mechanisms. Paclitaxel efficacy may also decrease when coadministered with CYP2C8 inducers. Use caution and monitor. 9. Rifampin decreases paliperidone levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Paliperidone dosage may need to be increased when coadministered with strong inducers of both CYP3A4 and P-gp. 10. Rifampin reduces pantoprazole levels or efficacy by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Rifampin decreases parecoxib levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Rifampin reduces paromomycin levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Rifampin decreases pentobarbital levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Rifampin reduces phenobarbital levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Rifampin decreases phenytoin levels or efficacy by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Rifampin reduces pimavanserin levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration if possible. Monitor for reduced efficacy, and consider increasing the pimavanserin dosage if necessary. 17. Rifampin decreases pimozide levels or efficacy by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Rifampin reduces pioglitazone levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Rifampin increases pitavastatin levels by decreasing metabolism. Do not exceed 2 mg/day of pitavastatin. Use caution and monitor. 20. Rifampin decreases pitolisant levels or efficacy by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pitolisant exposure decreases by 50% with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the pitolisant dosage by half. 21. Rifampin reduces polatuzumab vedotin levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease unconjugated MMAE AUC. Use caution and monitor. 22. Ponatinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 23. Rifampin reduces posaconazole levels or efficacy by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Rifampin increases pravastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 25. Rifampin decreases prednisolone levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 26. Rifampin reduces prednisone levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 27. Pretomanid increases rifampin levels or efficacy through unspecified mechanisms. Monitor for drug-related adverse effects when coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 28. Rifampin decreases primidone levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Probenecid increases rifampin levels or efficacy through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration increases rifampin concentration, potentially raising toxicity risk. Monitor for adverse reactions during coadministration. 30. Rifampin reduces propafenone levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Rifampin decreases propranolol levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Rifampin reduces quinine levels or efficacy by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Rifampin decreases rabeprazole levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Rifampin reduces raltegravir levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor. 35. Rifampin decreases ramelteon levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Rifampin reduces rasagiline levels or efficacy by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Rifampin is a relatively weak CYP1A2 inducer; caution is advised. Use caution and monitor. 37. Rifampin decreases riociguat levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Data for dose adjustment are unavailable. 38. Rifampin reduces risperidone levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Rifampin decreases ritonavir levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 40. Rifampin reduces rivaroxaban levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with drugs that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers. If coadministration is necessary, consider increasing the rivaroxaban dose. 41. Rifampin decreases romidepsin levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 42. Rifampin reduces ropinirole levels or efficacy by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Rifampin increases rosuvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 44. Rifampin decreases ruxolitinib levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Rifampin reduces ruxolitinib topical levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Rifampin increases sacubitril/valsartan levels or efficacy through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Coadministration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 47. Sarecycline increases rifampin levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, which may require dosage reduction when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 48. Rifampin reduces saxagliptin levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Rifampin decreases seladelpar levels or efficacy by increasing metabolism. Monitor biochemical response (e.g., ALP and bilirubin) when initiating rifampin during seladelpar treatment. Use caution and monitor. 50. Rifampin reduces selegiline levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Rifampin decreases selexipag levels or efficacy by increasing metabolism. Coadministration with rifampin, a CYP2C8, UGT1A3, and 2B7 inducer, reduces exposure to selexipag's active metabolite by 50%. Increase selexipag dose up to twice the typical dose if coadministered with rifampin. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Rifampin reduces sildenafil levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Potent CYP3A4 inducers are expected to cause substantial decreases in sildenafil plasma levels. Use caution and monitor. 53. Rifampin decreases silodosin levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 54. Rifampin increases simvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 55. Rifampin reduces sirolimus levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 56. Sodium bicarbonate decreases rifampin levels or efficacy through mechanisms involving reduced absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. Use caution and monitor. 57. Rifampin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Antibiotics decrease efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor. 58. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases rifampin toxicity through mechanisms involving fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor. 59. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases rifampin toxicity through mechanisms involving fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor. 60. Sparsentan decreases rifampin levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Sparsentan, a CYP2B6 inducer, reduces the efficacy of CYP2B6 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 61. Stiripentol increases rifampin levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Stiripentol is both a CYP2B6 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Rifampin reduces streptomycin levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 63. Rifampin decreases sufentanil levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers may decrease sufentanil levels and efficacy, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in patients with physical dependence. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentration. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 64. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid increases rifampin levels or efficacy by decreasing metabolism. Probenecid, an OAT1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of drugs dependent on OAT1/3 for elimination. Monitor more frequently for adverse reactions associated with rifampin. Use caution and monitor. 65. Rifampin reduces suvorexant levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease suvorexant efficacy. If an increased dose is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. Use caution and monitor. 66. Rifampin decreases tacrolimus levels or efficacy via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 67. Rifampin reduces tadalafil levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. For patients with erectile dysfunction, monitor response to tadalafil carefully due to potential decreased effectiveness. Use caution and monitor. 68. Rifampin decreases tamoxifen levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 69. Rifampin reduces tasimelteon levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Use caution and monitor. 70. Rifampin decreases teniposide levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 71. Rifampin reduces terbinafine levels or efficacy by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP1A2 and CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
